title: Manually driven observation-publication test races the production five-second fence deadline under parallel gate load
outcome: Manually driven observation-publication test races the production five-second fence deadline under parallel gate load
acceptance: Both observation-persistence fences measure their deadline on the state's existing Engram budget clock, through PersistFence::new_with_clock, and the observation step polls each fence on that fence's own clock. In production that clock is Real and the deadline stays 5 s; no production deadline, dispatch path, durability rule or published state changes.

A deterministic witness, RED before and GREEN after: in the observation publication fixture on a scripted clock, advancing that clock past 5 s before the write resolves the observation fence as Deadline and records failed tracking. That is also the control that a genuinely expired fence still fails. Without the advance, elapsed wall time cannot expire the fixture's fences.

observation_publication_late_start_ack_cannot_ack_the_new_terminal_image keeps every existing assertion: late start ACK versus the terminal image, and Running then Passed durability. No deadline inflation, sleep, synthetic load, ignore or skip is added. The test_run_observation* and persist_fence suites stay green.
A focused run plus the default full gate in the normal queue, a clean review pair, then one READY to Merger2.
